# I197 fresh discovery: completed bounded screen

2026-10-12. **NO VIABLE TARGET IN THIS ROUND.** Eight substantial findings remain accepted, two remain to be found. No nomination, independent acceptance, staging, commit, publication or shared-ledger edit is claimed. This completed record supersedes the initial PARTIAL prose. The interrupted run's authenticated reading was useful provenance, not an inherited mathematical result.

## Scope and screening decision

The controlling [I197 brief](iteration197-fresh-discovery-brief.md), [original I196 brief](iteration196-fresh-discovery-brief.md), and [parent correction](i196-fresh-discovery-parent-checkpoint.md) were read in full. The original assertion that all three families were unscreened is not used. E183/local-ear, J194/J193, J195, Q164, affine fullness, (T), and universal exchange were not reopened. The I196 stubs and unrelated I31 edit were preserved byte-for-byte against the inherited six-file baseline.

* **026 was fully screened.** All five proof sections of the pinned manuscript were read, including the general mixed moments, prime deletion, box singular-series average, detector bound and high-dimensional cancellation. The complete preprint tree and catalogue identify one manuscript for this family; no separate 026 companion was located in those metadata. The bibliography and adjacent source operations were checked for the precise prior-art boundary.
* **084 and 020 were excluded as instructed.** The parent correction records I36/I37's geometric work and I07/I99's squarefree overlaps, including `cor:separable-products`. Their proofs were not rederived or nominated.
* **No replacement family was selected or examined.** I197 permits at most two, rather than requiring the quota to be filled. This run completed both analytic routes in the assigned first family. A broad catalogue-title query was truncated and was not a substantive screen of other families. This verdict is limited to the present round; it is not an assertion that the rest of the catalogue has no targets.

Overlap searches used mathematical operations as well as titles: prime/gap frequency, chains, prime-free intervals, moment bounds, sieve weights, cancellation, and marked moments. Reports, reviews and dispatch JSON were searched. Hits were dispatch/history references, unrelated spectral gaps, and the earlier prime-factor/parity lanes; none of the inspected relevant hits supplied the chain argument below. A broader search also hit many frozen catalogue copies; these are provenance duplicates, not prior mathematical analyses. No missing keyword or absent family number is used to infer novelty. Search scopes and input hashes are in the [authentication record](../experiments/i197_fresh_discovery/input-authentication.json).

## What the mathematical work establishes

The [complete analytic record](../experiments/i197_fresh_discovery/analytic-attempt.md) proves this **technical deduction** from the accepted 026 operations:

For each C>0 and integer ell>=1, some finite B>C and eta>0 satisfy, for all sufficiently large N,

`#{1<=n<=N-ell : C log p_{n+j}<p_{n+j+1}-p_{n+j}<=B log p_{n+j} for every 0<=j<ell} >= eta N`.

Thus an arbitrary fixed length of consecutive large gaps has positive ordinary lower index density, with a nonprescribed finite upper bound. The proof uses many small detector windows separated by suppressed blocks. A first/second-moment score charges both multiple primes in a detector window and primes in a separating block. Positive score forces a run of the required number of isolated, consecutive primes. The accepted fourth moment then converts weighted mass into ordinary starts, and strip-length multiplicity gives prime-index density.

This is not derived merely by intersecting positive-density sets, and it uses no joint prime lower estimate. The exact finite-union reduction, parameter order, constants, boundary handling and counterexample to the density-only inference are written out in the analytic record.

The distinct second route tries to put a prime in each prescribed small window and suppress everything between. It would yield arbitrary prescribed narrow normalized-gap boxes, but the source has only one genuine prime mark. Its pair and higher divisor majorants give upper bounds; they do not provide the needed lower mass for a product of prime counts. The record states sufficient estimates J1-J3 and supplies an explicit mutually exclusive-occupancy countermodel to the attempted marginal-to-joint inference. This route is incomplete, not a theorem.

## Contribution gate and primary comparison

The [literature record](../sources/i197_fresh_discovery/literature.md) separates retrieved source statements from inference. The primary comparisons were read before settling the routes and rechecked against the final claims:

* Ford–Maynard–Tao, arXiv:1511.04468v1, Theorem 1 and section 3: extremal chains of very large gaps; its page 7 first/second-moment and close-pair removal argument is direct methodological prior art for our extraction.
* Bazzanella–Languasco–Zaccagnini, arXiv:0809.2967v1, Theorems 3, 5 and 6: integer-start and prime-start frequencies are distinct; its small-threshold prime-start theorem is not an all-threshold chain-density statement.
* Mastrostefano, arXiv:1812.11784v1, Theorem 1.1 and section 3: positive proportion with a prescribed total count in one sufficiently short interval. It does not supply prescribed joint occupancy under the suppression weight.

The technical chain statement differs from those inspected theorem statements in its counting measure. Nevertheless, its analytic content is already provided by 026's lower operations. Passing to finitely many cells is an expansion of the source box average; the extraction uses the classical first/second-moment method. No new distribution estimate or cancellation construction has been supplied. **It therefore fails the substantial-contribution gate even without a demonstrated verbatim literature duplicate.** Search absence would not change that conclusion.

The narrow-box route has a plausible substantive missing lower estimate, but no proof of it. Neither a conditional reduction nor a failed attempt can increase the finding count. Both independent gates remain with the parent for any future nomination.

## Deliverables and limits

The [reading/failure log](../experiments/i197_fresh_discovery/reading-and-failures.md) corrects the stale source-reading prose and records limited PDF reading, truncations, unavailable references, changed parent metadata, and preservation checks. The [authentication JSON](../experiments/i197_fresh_discovery/input-authentication.json) binds corpus URLs, labels, reading scopes and SHA-256 values. Only the eight corpus files read in full are retained; no partially read PDF is stored as a full-read source copy.

This is an unsealed written research record. No research code, computational experiment, test suite, snapshot, seal, historical replay, agent creation, ledger edit, staging, commit or publication was performed. Source retrieval, text searches and hashing were used. The proof is a self-reviewed deduction under the user's source stipulation, not an independent acceptance PASS.

## Written mathematical check

The parent read the completed analytic argument and the retained source's
weight construction, cancellation construction, mixed-moment statement,
box singular-series lemma and square-evaluation proof. Under the user's
stipulation accepting these source operations, the fixed-chain deduction
passes this scoped written check:

For each C>0 and integer ell>=1 there are finite B>C and eta>0 such that,
for every sufficiently large N, at least eta N starting indices n have
ell consecutive gaps all between C log p and B log p, with the chain
ending by p_N. B and eta may depend on C and ell.

The source box lemma allows the finite-cell decomposition of disjoint
suppressed and detector regions. The single-prime marked formula supplies
the two first moments, and the six-factor unmarked upper bound supplies
the detector-pair cost. All dimensions and cells are fixed before X grows.
The extraction score is

`Y = T - (r+1)R - (r-1)U - (r-1)`, with r=ell+1.

If there is no run of r singleton detector cells, the combinatorial
inequalities a>=T-2R, b<=R and a<=(r-1)(b+U+1) give Y<=0.
The stated choices H=2r, delta<=1/[2c(r+1)], epsilon=1/(4r)
leave positive weighted score. Two Cauchy-Schwarz applications use the
fixed-family second moment of W; they do not require its uniformity as
epsilon tends to zero. Charging at most the fixed strip length per selected
first prime gives ordinary index density. The strict q delta>C pays the
integer endpoints and replacement of log X by log p.

The second route is correctly left conditional. Its J1-J3 estimates would
produce prescribed narrow gap boxes, but the source permits only one
genuine prime mark. Upper divisor majorants cannot supply the joint
positive lower bound J1. The mutually exclusive-window model invalidates
the proposed inference from marginal moments; it is a counterexample to
that inference, not a claimed model of primes.

This is a parent written check of a technical deduction, not the two
independent acceptance reviews required for a substantial nomination.
